references_named: Bruce Nauman (neon window/spiral signs, The True Artist Helps the World by Revealing Mystic Truths, 1967)
rationale: The mechanism is the argument (P1): CSS bidi-override over a reversed DOM string literally stages the front-of-glass/back-of-glass split the piece is about, and the small find-box makes the divergence demonstrable rather than asserted. The Nauman reference is precise, and the deliberate inversion of Scrittura Speculare is an elegant way to claim a coherent lineage without duplication — the two works are presented as the two sides of the same pane. Voice is dry, intelligent, restrained; ethics (CC BY-SA, no network, no tracking) are explicit and non-negotiable. The work passes every gate.
reservations: Novelty sits below the other scores: unicode-bidi reversal is a long-known web trick, and Trojan Source (2021) is a well-publicized reading of exactly this gap. The piece's originality is almost entirely in the Nauman framing and the inverse-Scrittura pairing rather than in the mechanism itself, so the catalogue gains a smart execution more than a new ontology. A literal print of just the front text would already convey the idea to a willing reader; the medium dependency is real but thin compared to, say, the API-driven or canvas-paint exemplars in the catalogue.
revision_suggestion: To lift novelty toward the strong threshold, give the work more web-mechanism load: e.g. drive the marquee through actual bidi interaction (live LRM/RLM embedding characters that the engine must parse), make a screen-reader path demonstrably read the reversed string while a visible 'as read aloud' line crawls under the neon, or have the page compare a fetched search-engine-style snippet of its own URL against the rendered text. Any of these would make the mechanism do more work than the framing currently does.
